input_files: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx - the firm's practice note on mechanics lien claims on private works: preliminary notice, completion and the notice of completion, the time to record, the amount of the lien, waivers and releases, the 90 day enforcement period, the owner's remedies, and the counting conventions the office uses

claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx - the seven claims of mechanics lien recorded against the property, transcribed from the recorder's copies with each proof of service affidavit and the exhibits two claimants attached

owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx - the owner's project file: the preliminary notices received, the waivers and releases received with each payment application, the owner's payments to the direct contractor with retention, and the subcontractor list with subcontract values
dk_subcontractor_payments.csv - the direct contractor's subcontractor payment ledger for the job, every check issued to a subcontractor with its payment application, amount, and bank status

completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx - the notice of completion as recorded, the construction manager's completion memorandum, the email exchange among the owner, the direct contractor, and the firm, and the civil index and recorder searches
output_files: lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx - the lien analysis workbook with the page for the partner, the governing dates, the preliminary notice and deadline tests, the waivers read against the payment ledger, each claim built up to its enforceable amount, the standing and bond for each claim, and the note to the partner
task_instruction:
Nadia at Piedmont Ridge wants the Larkspur Crossing liens dealt with before the refinance closes on November 20, and Marguerite has to tell her by the end of the month which claims we demand released and which the bank will make us bond. I'm the paralegal on the Piedmont Ridge account at Ferraro Whitcombe in Sacramento, California, and the first analysis on every lien file the office defends starts with me. I am in trial in Redding through the 16th, so I am handing this one to you because you have worked mechanics lien claims in this office for years and can read a waiver form against a check register without the Code open beside you. The file is in the folder: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx, claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx, owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx, dk_subcontractor_payments.csv, and completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx. The claims are our transcriptions of the recorder's copies with whatever each claimant attached, and the payments file is what Dunmore-Kettle's controller sent when Marguerite asked for it.

Build the analysis as one workbook named lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx. The first tab is what Marguerite reads: for each recorded claim, whether the claimant has lien rights at all, whether the claim was recorded in time, what the waivers on file do to it, the amount the claimant could actually enforce against the property, what we do about it, and what a release bond would have to be for each lien we cannot clear. Behind it I want the dates worked from the notice of completion under the practice note, the preliminary notices and the waivers checked claimant by claimant against the payments, and each enforceable amount built up so that Marguerite can follow every dollar to the claim or the ledger it came from. Put a note to Marguerite on the last tab with anything the file leaves open and anything that cuts against what Nadia expects. Nadia's position with the bank is that every claim is either late, waived, or Dunmore-Kettle's to answer, and if the record says otherwise Marguerite needs to hear it from us first. I need the workbook by Tuesday, October 20.

rubric.description: The deliverable is a single workbook named exactly lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx whose first worksheet states the standing of each of the 7 recorded claims.

The first worksheet's release bonds required total reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the claim-by-claim standing behind it, or a sum over the same per-claim bonds alike, standing at $399,425.55.
The last day for a claimant other than the direct contractor to record is stated as 09/21/2026 because the thirtieth day after the notice of completion fell on a Saturday.
Ostrowski Electric's claim recorded 09/21/2026 is found timely.
Calder Drywall's claim recorded 09/22/2026 is found untimely.
Norcal Rebar is found to have no lien rights because its preliminary notice was given to the direct contractor and never to the owner.
Tallac Concrete's lien is found expired because no action was commenced within 90 days after its recording.
Hedrick & Sons' enforceable amount is stated as $33,982.19 on the first worksheet.
Kastner Mechanical's enforceable amount is stated as $159,145 on the first worksheet.
Bautista Painting's enforceable amount is stated as $8,125 on the first worksheet.
The first worksheet carries all 7 recorded claims, 3 of them routed to a demand for release.
The amount the claimants could enforce against the property is stated as $262,729.19 on the first worksheet.
The recorded amount of the claims to demand released is stated as $99,830.00.
The three claims that cannot be enforced are routed to a demand for release under section 8482 as the first step.
The note to Marguerite is the last worksheet.
The note tells Marguerite that the direct contractor can still record a claim until 10/19/2026.
The workbook wrongly treats the HVAC subcontractor's conditional waiver through 07/31/2026 as releasing the July payment although check 4460 was stopped.
The workbook wrongly treats the painting subcontractor's unconditional waiver through 07/31/2026 as ineffective for want of payment although section 8134 makes it effective when signed.
The workbook wrongly measures a release bond by the enforceable amount although section 8424(b) sets it at 125 percent of the claim as recorded.
The workbook wrongly includes the lumber supplier's April deliveries in its enforceable amount although its late preliminary notice reaches back only twenty days before it was given.
The workbook wrongly starts the 30 days at the completion date rather than at the recording of the notice of completion.
The workbook wrongly treats the site concrete subcontractor's lien release letter as releasing the May balance although it is not in the statutory form.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as a lien analysis the partner can act on with the bank's counsel.
